blocks.h2: Time to Repair or Replace a Faucet?

tiles.body: Original faucets in 1990s and 2000s homes start dripping and loosening around the same time.
A worn cartridge or seal. Quick to fix on a good faucet.
Mineral scale from well water builds on spouts and aerators.
A loose supply line or a tired shutoff valve.

bodies: Swapping the kitchen faucet is a popular upgrade in Algonquin homes. We install pull-downs, touchless models, pot fillers and filtered-water taps, and repair the ones you want to keep.
We check the shutoffs and supply lines on every install. Original valves from the 1990s can stick or start dripping once they're turned, so we replace them while the sink is open.
Beyond the faucet: sink drains, dishwasher hookups, refrigerator and ice maker lines, disposals and gas lines for ranges. For remodels, we move or add plumbing to fit new islands and layouts.

Clogged sink? See [drain cleaning](/algonquin/drain-cleaning). Disposal trouble? See [garbage disposal repair](/algonquin/garbage-disposal-installation-repair). Gas range? See [gas line installation](/algonquin/gas-line-installation).

img.alt: Plumbing under a double kitchen sink: white PVC drain and P-trap, braided supply lines with chrome shutoff valves, and a garbage disposal

bodies: We install sinks, faucets, toilets, showerheads, tub fillers, laundry tubs and outdoor spigots, from a single swap to a whole bathroom remodel. Each install includes connections, new shutoffs where needed and a leak check.

Picked out your own fixtures? Send us the make and model to confirm the fit. For toilets, see [toilet installation](/algonquin/toilet-installation-repair). For showers, see [shower repair](/algonquin/shower-repair).

blocks.h2: Faucets and Fixtures in Algonquin Homes
blocks.intro: With a median home built in 1994, Algonquin is full of fixtures reaching the end of their first life.

items.body: When one original faucet fails, the rest are usually close. Replacing several in one visit saves time.
Minerals shorten cartridge life. A working softener protects new fixtures.
Many homeowners are remodeling original bathrooms now. We handle the plumbing side.

blocks.h2: Faucet and Fixture Questions From Algonquin Homeowners

items.q: Should I replace all my original faucets at once?
items.preview: If they're the same age and starting to fail, it often makes sense.
items.answer: If they're original to a 1990s or 2000s home and starting to drip, replacing them together saves trips. We'll give you one flat price for all of them.

items.q: Can you install a faucet I bought online?
items.preview: Yes. Send us the make and model.
items.answer: Yes. Send us the make and model and we'll confirm it fits before the visit.

items.q: Why is there white crust on my faucet?
items.answer: Minerals in the water dry on the faucet and build up. Vinegar removes light scale. A softener prevents most of it.

items.q: Should I fix or replace a dripping faucet?
items.preview: Fix a good faucet. Replace a worn-out one.
items.answer: If it's a quality faucet with a worn cartridge, fix it. If it's a builder-grade model with corrosion or loose parts, replacement is often the better value.

items.q: What does faucet installation cost in Algonquin?
items.preview: It depends on the faucet and valves. The price comes first.
items.answer: It depends on the faucet, the shutoffs and supply lines and access. We quote a flat rate before we start.
